topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the structure, learning objectives, and interdisciplinary scope of the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of genetic regulation, cellular differentiation, and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how stepwise genetic and epigenetic alterations disrupt normal developmental differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign versus malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the histological characteristics, metastatic dissemination pathways, and clinical progression patterns distinguishing benign from malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification conventions
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the standardized terminology and naming rules used to categorize benign and malignant tumors based on their tissue origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the local and systemic processes through which tumor mass effects and metastatic spread cause organ failure, illness, and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across human populations and multicellular taxa
topics.groupedBecause: They examine cancer epidemiological patterns and mortality rates in humans while comparing tumor susceptibility across diverse multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss clinical cancer symptoms and evaluate the utility, histology, and limitations of various screening methods for early tumor detection.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and providing directions for upcoming practicals and lectures.
